sections.html:
The wait before a Nebraska landlord can go to court varies with the reason. Late rent carries a 7-day notice, a lease violation carries 14 or 30 days, dangerous conduct carries 5 days, and a month-to-month arrangement needs 30 days. All of it must be on paper.

ReasonWritten noticeCan the tenant fix it?
Rent not paid (76-1431(2))7 calendar daysYes, by paying within the 7 days
Material lease breach (76-1431(1))Ends no less than 30 days after receipt if not remedied in 14 daysYes, within 14 days
Same breach again within 6 months (76-1431(1))At least 14 daysNo cure period
Violent crime, illegal drug sales, threats to safety (76-1431(4))5 daysNo right to cure
Month-to-month, no cause (76-1437(2))30 days before the rental dateNot applicable
Week-to-week, no cause (76-1437(1))7 days before the end dateNot applicable

The notice just opens the process. Getting the tenant out still takes a court win.

Two statements belong in the notice. Rent is unpaid, and the landlord intends to terminate the rental agreement unless payment arrives within seven calendar days. Termination rights hinge on written notice of both.

Full payment inside the seven days leaves the landlord with nothing to terminate on. Rent still owed afterward lets the landlord end the agreement and head to court, as described below.

Seven here means calendar days, so weekends and holidays count. Save evidence of the delivery method and date, because the complaint has to show the notice requirements were met.

One notice carries both numbers. It describes what the tenant did or failed to do. Termination follows at least 30 days after receipt, unless the tenant corrects the problem within 14 days.

Covered are a failure of the tenant's duties that seriously affects health and safety, and any material breach of the lease. Where repairs, payment of damages or another step can fix it, and the tenant gets that done before the notice date, the lease survives.

  • A return of the same problem inside six months can be ended on written notice of 14 days or more, without a fresh chance to cure.
  • Damages and an injunction are also available to the landlord for noncompliance.
  • Willful noncompliance can bring reasonable attorney's fees.

The short five-day track is for serious conduct by the tenant, a household member, a guest or anyone the tenant controls: violent crime, illegal sale of a controlled substance, or other acts that endanger other tenants, the landlord or the landlord's staff. Curing is not an option.

The statute gives examples: assault or a threat of it, unlawful use of a firearm or other weapon, a controlled substance the tenant knew or should have known was present, and conduct that threatens or causes property damage. Incidents behind the suit must be spelled out in the complaint.

An innocent tenant has a shield. If an outsider, not the tenant or a household member, is responsible and the tenant seeks a protective order or reports to law enforcement, the landlord cannot rely on this notice. Someone who commits domestic violence is not covered.

sections.h2: Ending a month-to-month tenancy without a reason
sections.html:
Landlord or tenant may end a month-to-month tenancy with a written notice that gives 30 days or more before the rental date it names. For week-to-week the minimum is seven days before the termination date.

Without a stated term, Nebraska treats a lease as monthly, or weekly for a roomer who pays weekly. Inherited a house with an occupant and no written lease? Expect that default to apply.

Staying on after the term or after termination, without consent, exposes a tenant to a possession suit. A willful holdover in bad faith can add up to three months' periodic rent or threefold actual damages, whichever is greater, along with reasonable attorney's fees.

Once the notice period ends, the landlord files a complaint for restitution at the district or county court clerk's office. The complaint states the legal basis for possession, the facts, a fairly accurate description of the premises, and the steps taken to meet the notice rules.

  1. A summons and a copy of the complaint go out from the court. Service has to be made within three days and the return is due within five days, with nonjudicial days excluded from both counts.
  2. The judge decides the case alone, with no jury.
  3. A judgment against the tenant forfeits the rental agreement.
  4. If the landlord asks, the court issues a writ of restitution that orders the constable or sheriff to return possession, on a date within ten days of the writ.

Only an officer carrying out a writ can return possession. No notice, by itself, changes who may stay in the house.

Landlords cannot answer a code complaint with a rent increase, lost services, or a possession suit or threat. That covers complaints to a housing or building code agency about a health and safety violation, and joining a tenants' union. A tenant who proves it has a defense to the possession case.

Exceptions let the landlord still sue. These are a violation caused mainly by the tenant's lack of reasonable care, rent that is behind, and compliance that would require work depriving the tenant of the unit. Reasonable rent increases stay allowed.

When a tenant dies, the landlord has ten days to make a reasonable attempt to reach the person the tenant named for retrieving belongings. That person gets 20 days after contact to say the property will be claimed, then 20 more days to take it away.

You have three options when a tenant lives in the house: finish the notice and court steps and then list, sell around the tenant, or find a buyer who accepts the house as is. The lease, the case's progress and your closing deadline decide which.

  • Save the lease, rent ledger, each notice and delivery proof.
  • Check for an open complaint, judgment or writ, since a buyer will weigh those papers.
  • Deeds recorded July 18, 2026 or later carry the $3.32 per $1,000 documentary stamp tax and need a Form 521.

Cash Home Buyers can purchase a house while an eviction is underway, so you need not wait for a judgment and writ. This page outlines notice rules from Nebraska's Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act and is not legal advice. Before serving a notice, read the current statutes or consult a Nebraska attorney.

faqs.q: How long is a Nebraska eviction notice for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Seven calendar days after a written notice of nonpayment and intent to terminate. Paying within that time stops the termination.

faqs.q: Can a Nebraska landlord evict without going to court?
faqs.a: No. The landlord must file a complaint for restitution, and only a constable or sheriff holding a writ of restitution can return possession.

faqs.q: How long does a tenant have to leave after a judgment?
faqs.a: The writ's possession date must fall within ten days of its issue. The court issues it after judgment when the landlord asks.

faqs.q: What notice ends a month-to-month tenancy in Nebraska?
faqs.a: A written notice given 30 or more days ahead of the rental date it names. Either party may send it, and no reason is needed.

faqs.q: Does the tenant get a chance to fix a lease violation?
faqs.a: Usually, with 14 days to remedy before the agreement ends 30 or more days after receipt. A repeat within six months allows 14 days' notice with no cure, and violent or dangerous conduct allows five days' notice with no cure.
